correctness.rationale: The frozen geometric and numerical assertions check out. The repaired finding in /workspace/repairs/4 also identifies the local resolution with the normalized point blow-up. In the affine vertex chart the strict-transform equation is Q^3=r^3 P. The chart T^3=P, Q=rT is finite over it, and off r=0 its inverse is T=Q/r. At branch directions (P,Q) are analytic parameters by transversality and (T,r) are regular parameters of the new chart. Elsewhere on r=0 the nonzero T derivative and the smooth conic give regular charts. The exceptional fiber is the reduced connected triple cover of the conic and is one-dimensional, so no extra component of the finite smooth chart lies over r=0. The charts are compatible by the weights of r and T; they give the normalization near the fiber. Riemann–Hurwitz at 18 index-3 directions gives genus 16, hence no rational exceptional (-1)-component. The line of the ambient blow-up restricted to the curve is its normal line, giving rho*O(-2) and square -6; independently D^2=4*3 and the 18 simple basepoints subtract 18. The cyclic pushforward on the conic is O⊕O(-6)⊕O(-12), yielding h^1 of the conormal powers as stated, not a formal-neighborhood argument. The cyclic cover and S_Q are normal by the isolated hypersurface singularities criterion; the 18 basepoint exceptionals map onto lines, not into the exceptional divisor of the resolution. Compactly supported Euler additivity gives 70 via fibers of sizes 3,1,0 and affine lines, and subtracting the 12 ordinary cubic-cone contributions from 459-70 gives 293. Running python3 -B /workspace/repairs/4/verify.py verifies the transverse conic and incidences over Q(zeta), normal-bundle arithmetic and both Euler decompositions, not the normalization argument itself.
